What a /31 means

A /31 has two addresses and no network or broadcast address (RFC 3021), so every address is usable. It is the modern choice for point-to-point links.

The prefix length is the number of leading bits that identify the network. A /31 uses 31 network bits and leaves 1 host bits, so the block contains 2 addresses. Usable hosts: 2(32−31) = 2; /31 and /32 are special cases.

Configuration examples

Cisco IOS

interface Vlan10
 ip address 192.168.1.0 255.255.255.254
!
access-list 10 permit 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.1

Juniper Junos

set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 192.168.1.0/31

Linux

ip addr add 192.168.1.0/31 dev eth0

Addresses shown are examples from private or documentation space. Replace them with your own plan.

FAQ

How many usable hosts are in a /31?

2. A /31 uses both addresses on point-to-point links (RFC 3021).

What is the subnet mask for /31?

255.255.255.254. The wildcard mask, used in ACLs and OSPF network statements, is 0.0.0.1.
